subject: chemistry

moments.title: Boyle's chemistry of fire
moments.body:
Boyle establishes that combustion needs air. He shows a candle in a sealed jar goes out, and a mouse in the same jar suffocates. He concludes air contains something essential to burning and breathing.

He does not name the substance. The Sceptical Chymist (1661) is a manifesto for chemistry as an experimental discipline.
moments.takeaway: Boyle frames burning as a chemical process needing a specific component of air.

moments.title: Stahl's phlogiston theory
moments.body:
Stahl unifies combustion, calcination of metals and respiration under one concept: all involve release of a hypothetical substance called phlogiston. Combustible materials are rich in phlogiston; non-combustible materials lack it.

The theory works coherently for most observations — until people start weighing things carefully.
moments.takeaway: Phlogiston unifies fire, rust and breathing. A productive but ultimately wrong theory.

moments.title: Lavoisier's sealed-vessel experiments
moments.body:
Lavoisier conducts a deposition: 'I deposit the following note... so that I can claim its discovery as my own if others should make the same observations.' He had noted: a metal calcined in a sealed vessel does not change the total weight; on opening the vessel, air rushes in, and the metal's calx weighs more than the original metal.

The weight gained equals the air that rushed in. Burning ADDS mass from air — it doesn't release phlogiston.
moments.takeaway: Quantitative observation overturns a major theory. Lavoisier is staking a claim.

moments.title: Lavoisier announces the new theory
moments.body:
Lavoisier publishes 'Réflexions sur le Phlogistique', a full attack on phlogiston theory. Combustion is the combination of substances with oxygen. The decrease in air volume during burning equals the oxygen consumed.

The old guard resists. Priestley dies in 1804 still defending phlogiston. By 1810 phlogiston is dead among working chemists.
moments.takeaway: A scientific revolution takes about 25 years to be accepted, despite clean experimental evidence.

now.title: Combustion today
now.body:
We understand combustion at multiple levels. Macroscopic: fuel + oxygen → CO2 + H2O + energy. Detailed: hundreds of elementary radical reactions, modelled by chemical kinetics software. Internal combustion engines, jet engines, rockets — all designed using combustion chemistry.

Low-temperature combustion (HCCI engines), oxy-fuel combustion (for carbon capture), hydrogen combustion (water as the only product) are active research areas.
now.open_questions: Can we capture CO2 at the point of combustion at scale and at low cost? Can hydrogen replace fossil fuels in industrial-scale combustion? How do soot and aerosol particles form and what's their full climate impact?

reflection: Stahl's phlogiston theory was wrong but useful for nearly a century. It made predictions and could be tested. Lavoisier's theory replaced it because of mass measurements that Stahl's contemporaries couldn't have made. How do we treat theories that are 'productively wrong' in their own time?
